images.title: A caved in quadrilateral still makes 360°
images.purpose: Shows a quadrilateral with one corner that caves in, split by its inside diagonal into two triangles, with angles 30°, 40°, 50° and 240° adding up to 360°.
images.composition: Plain white background, the main object large and centred with wide empty margins, no scenery, no characters, no extra decoration. One large arrowhead shaped quadrilateral in the centre, split by its inside diagonal into two shaded triangles.
images.exact_structure: One concave quadrilateral ABCD in dark outline shaped like an arrowhead pointing up: B is the tip at the top, A at the bottom left, C at the bottom right, and D is the caved in corner, inside the shape between A and C, lower than B. The diagonal BD is a dashed dark line from B down to D, lying inside the shape. Triangle ABD on the left is lightly filled teal (#0072B2) and triangle CBD on the right is lightly filled amber (#E69F00). Angle arcs in reddish purple (#CC79A7) inside the shape: 30° at A, 40° at B, 50° at C, and a large arc for the reflex angle at D, labelled 240°. Only D is lettered, just below the caved in corner. Under the shape, centred, the line 30° + 40° + 50° + 240° = 360°. Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: Even when one corner caves in, the inside diagonal makes two triangles, so the angles still add up to 360°.
